title: fetchProjects catch block swallows error with no user feedback
detail: Line 116: `.catch(function() { setLoadingProjects(false); })` — if the projects API call fails, loadingProjects flips to false and the user sees 'No projects found.' (the empty state from line 257). They have no way to distinguish 'zero projects exist' from 'the API call failed'. No toast is shown.
recommendedFix: Add toast.show('err', 'Failed to load projects') in the catch block before setLoadingProjects(false). Consider also rendering a retry button or distinct error state instead of the same empty-state message.

title: Submit button not disabled during createRfpProject Promise.all — double-submit possible
detail: Lines 143-187: handleSubmit sets submitting=true and the button on line 404 correctly checks `disabled: submitting`. However, if createRfpPackage succeeds but the project-linking Promise.all (line 179) fails, setSubmitting(false) is never called in the .then path — only in the outer .catch (line 185). This means on a partial failure (package created, some project links failed), the button stays disabled permanently until navigation. The user cannot retry the project linking. Additionally, after a successful submit with 0 projects, navigate fires but setSubmitting(false) is also never called — the navigate hides the issue but if the navigation were to fail for any reason, the button would be stuck.
evidence: createRfpPackage(payload).then(function(record) { ... if (selectedIds.length === 0) { toast.show('ok', ...); navigate(...); return; } ... Promise.all(promises).then(function() { toast.show('ok', ...); navigate(...); }); }).catch(function(e) { toast.show('err', ...); setSubmitting(false); });
recommendedFix: Add setSubmitting(false) in a .finally() on the outer promise chain, or in both the success and error paths. Also handle the case where Promise.all fails: add a .catch to the Promise.all that surfaces a partial-success toast and calls setSubmitting(false).

title: RFP project links use inline @odata.bind strings instead of portalApi helpers
detail: Lines 173-176: `createRfpProject({ 'dcfg_rfp_package_id@odata.bind': '/dcfg_rfp_packages(' + rfpId + ')', 'dcfg_project_id@odata.bind': '/dcfg_projects(' + projId + ')' })` — constructs OData bind strings manually with hardcoded entity set names. The rest of the codebase uses the `odataBind()` helper from portalApi.js and `EntitySets.*` constants. Manual construction is fragile: if the entity set name ever changes (e.g. dcfg_rfp_packages vs a rename), only portalApi needs updating — but this inline string would be missed.
recommendedFix: Import odataBind and EntitySets from portalApi.js. Replace inline binds with: ...odataBind('dcfg_rfp_package_id', EntitySets.rfpPackages, rfpId), ...odataBind('dcfg_project_id', EntitySets.projects, projId).

title: handleSubmit payload does not set dcfg_created_by_email
detail: Lines 147-154: the createRfpPackage payload includes dcfg_name, dcfg_trades, dcfg_scope_description, dcfg_deadline, dcfg_active_flag, and optionally dcfg_total_estimated_value — but does not include dcfg_created_by_email. Both ContractComposer (line 482) and MsaComposer (line 156) set this field on their respective create payloads. Without it, the RFP record has no attribution to the creating user.
evidence: var payload = { dcfg_name: name.trim(), dcfg_trades: trades.trim(), dcfg_scope_description: scope.trim(), dcfg_deadline: deadline || null, dcfg_active_flag: true };
recommendedFix: Import usePortalUser, destructure userEmail, add `dcfg_created_by_email: userEmail` to the payload.

title: No audit log written on RFP package creation
detail: handleSubmit creates the RFP package and links projects but never calls writeAuditLog. Both ContractComposer (line 708) and MsaComposer (line 231) write audit logs after creation. The RFP create path is the only wizard that skips audit logging entirely.
recommendedFix: Import writeAuditLog and AuditActionType from portalApi.js. After successful creation, call writeAuditLog({ targetTable: 'dcfg_rfp_package', targetRecordId: rfpId, actionType: AuditActionType.Created, performedBy: userEmail, newValue: 'RFP package created via wizard' }).catch(() => {}).

title: Uses var declarations and React.createElement instead of JSX — stylistic inconsistency with rest of SPA
detail: The entire file uses ES5-style `var` declarations (lines 11-22, 76-108) and `React.createElement` calls instead of JSX (lines 26-67, 193-411). Every other wizard/composer in the SPA (ContractComposer, MsaComposer, NewProposalWizard) uses modern const/let and JSX syntax. This is a maintenance burden — the file is harder to read and modify. Not a functional bug, but a handoff cleanliness issue.
recommendedFix: Catalog only for this review. Future pass: convert to JSX + const/let to match the rest of the codebase.

title: Project selection checkboxes are div-based — not accessible as form controls
detail: Lines 261-287: each project option is a <div> with onClick and a visual checkbox (styled div). There is no actual <input type='checkbox'>, no role='checkbox', no aria-checked attribute. Keyboard users cannot tab to these items and screen readers cannot announce them as checkboxes. The visual-only checkbox div uses colors to indicate state but provides no semantic information.
evidence: React.createElement('div', { style: { width: '20px', height: '20px', borderRadius: '4px', ... }, ...}, isSelected ? '\u2713' : '')
recommendedFix: Add role='checkbox', aria-checked={isSelected}, tabIndex=0, and onKeyDown handler (Space/Enter to toggle) to each project option div. Alternatively, use actual <input type='checkbox'> elements.
